SADV5A-01.note: survivors=4; no cheap bound: all options positive, no sign/magnitude/monotone read from the stem (discriminant k^2-10k+21 is a solving step; 7 is one k, 21 is their product, 16 is neither). bank duplicate: sat-adv-hard-v3.batch.json AM3-07 (x^2 + (k+3)x + k+6 = 0, exactly one real solution, same (k+3) coefficient shape, discriminant as a quadratic in k); within-file pair with SADV5A-05 (same mechanism, discriminant quadratic in k).

SADV5A-02.note: survivors=3; magnitude: one root is 5/2 read off the stem and the other satisfies 4x+19=0 so |root|<5, |product|<12.5 kills D (-95); sign (positive times negative) kills nothing. Structural: B and D are a key x8 pair sharing numerator 95, C (-9/4) is the SUM of the roots. No bank duplicate of the factor-out-common-binomial mechanism.

SADV5A-03.note: survivors=4; convexity/chord: f(0) below the chord from (-4,43) to (3,22) gives f(0)<31, kills nothing; no lower bound without solving for a. No stem-number restatement among options. No bank duplicate (SADV-02, SADV2-01, SAM11-19 fit a quadratic from a vertex or symmetric pair, not three general points).

SADV5A-04.note: survivors=3; definitional extreme: D (4) is the un-shifted axis of f itself, and g is a non-trivial shift so the answer cannot equal it; a right shift moves the vertex right so answer>4 (kills D only). SADV5A-05.note: survivors=3; three-option cluster with one outlier: A,B,C are 9,10,15 (small sums of a few consecutive integers), D (-55) is the sign-and-magnitude outlier and dies. SADV5A-06.note: survivors=2; sign: sum -5/3 with one root +4 forces the other root negative, so the product c/3 is negative, kills A (28). Structural: B (-68) and C (-68/3) are a key/3 pair sharing numerator 68, D (-20) is 3*4*(-5/3) (sum used as the other root). Adjacent pair narrows to B/C. Near duplicate mechanism: sat-adv-v5.batch.json ADV5-14 (one root given, find the other via Vieta) and sat-adv-0918b.batch.json SADVB-07 (Vieta with a root relation, find c); non-unit leading coefficient is the only new element.

SADV5A-07.note: survivors=3; vertex value as ceiling: the second parabola is -2(x-4)^2+13 so every intersection y<=13, the sum of two y's <=26, kills C (65 = 5*13, the product); vertex floor of the first parabola (x-1)^2+4 gives sum>=8, kills nothing. A (13) is one of the two y-values. bank duplicate: sat-adv-v6.batch.json ADV6-08 (IDENTICAL first parabola y = x^2 - 2x + 5 against a second downward parabola, asks a y-coordinate of the intersection); also sat-adv-hard-v4.batch.json AM4-16 and sat-adv-v5.batch.json ADV5-09 (sum of y-coordinates of intersection points).

SADV5A-08.note: survivors=2; endpoint beyond landing: h=0 near t=8.6, so A (15) is after landing; D (17/2) is 136/16, the time the ball returns to launch height h=20 (mirror of t=0), read off without solving, so it cannot be a 260-ft time. Remaining B (5 = 2*2.5) and C. bank duplicate: sat-adv-v6.batch.json ADV6-17 (ball first at a height of 100 ft, -16t^2+80t+4: same quadratic-height-equals-value mechanism, first-time variant); sat-adv-hard-v4.batch.json AM4-17 and sat-adv-0918.kept.batch.json SADV-09 are the interval variants.

SADV5A-09.note: survivors=1; sign and magnitude: proportional coefficients a:b:6 = 2:-5:1 with scale factor 6 forces b negative and |b| > a (5 > 2), so a+b must be negative; kills A (12 = a alone), B (7), C (42). SADV5B-01.note: survivors=2; convexity: an increasing exponential gains more per unit than its average over the previous span, so f(3) > 36 + (36-16)/2 = 46 kills B (40.5); magnitude: b^2 = 2.25 so b < 2.25 and f(3) = 36b < 81 kills D (121.5 = 36*1.5^3). SADV5B-02.note: survivors=2; magnitude: three compounding periods of 8% decrease lie strictly between the two-period decrease (15.4, which is option B exactly) and the linear 24%; kills B (2 periods) and C (11.8 = 1.5 periods from 18/12). SADV5B-03.note: survivors=2; structural adjacent pair: A (7) and C (16) differ by exactly 9, the value that zeroes the denominator, so one is the sum with the extraneous root and the other without; the key is the smaller. B (15) is the sum of the squared-equation roots, D (36) their product, C (25) is (x+13) at the key. bank duplicate: sat-adv-hard-v1.batch.json AM-H-11 (sqrt(3x+1) = x-3), sat-adv-hard-v3.batch.json AM3-01 (sqrt(2x+22) = x-1), sat-adv-v5.batch.json ADV5-18, sat-adv-hard-v4.batch.json AM4-14, sat-adv-h3.kept.batch.json AH3-05, sat-adv-0918.batch.json SADV-08.

A (-244) is p(-1), C (84) is 3 + 81 (sign slip), B (-21) is neither. No bank duplicate: no sum-of-coefficients item exists in any batch.

Once the first division step x*(x^2-3x-4) is subtracted the remainder 6x+5 appears immediately, so this is easier than its framing. A (-123 = 7k - 4) and C (-143 = 7(-21) + 4, k from 21 + k = 0 with the 4x term dropped) remain with D. No bank duplicate of the constant-for-all-x difference mechanism (sat-adv-0918c.batch.json SADVC-03 and sat-adv-v6.batch.json ADV6-06 are plain coefficient matching).
